classification.difficultyReason: Eliminate each parameter, justify the explicitly supplied coordinate restrictions, and translate them into a whole line, closed segment and ray.

content.prompt: Different parametric representations may result in the same Cartesian equation. The graphical representation may be different, due to domain and range restrictions.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the Cartesian equation of $x=2-t$ and $y=t-1$ and sketch the graph.

answer.short: $x+y=1$. The graph is the whole straight line through $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$.
answer.worked:
$$t=2-x$$
Substituting into $y=t-1$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=(2-x)-1\\y&=1-x\\x+y&=1\end{aligned}$$
There are no domain or range restrictions, so the line extends in both directions.

spec.description: Whole line with continuation arrows, labelled unit intercepts and no grid. Ordinary source-blue marks use house black.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the Cartesian equation of the curve $(\sin^2t,\cos^2t)$. Explain why $0\le x\le1$ and $0\le y\le1$ and sketch the graph.

answer.short: $x+y=1$, with $0\le x\le1$ and $0\le y\le1$: the closed line segment from $(0,1)$ to $(1,0)$.
answer.worked:
Let $x=\sin^2t$ and $y=\cos^2t$. Using the Pythagorean identity,
$$\begin{aligned}x+y&=\sin^2t+\cos^2t\\x+y&=1.\end{aligned}$$
Since $0\le\sin^2t\le1$, we have $0\le x\le1$. Since $0\le\cos^2t\le1$, we have $0\le y\le1$. The graph is the segment joining $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$, including both endpoints.

spec.description: Closed descending segment with filled endpoints and labelled unit intercepts. No grid or continuation arrows. Ordinary source-blue marks use house black.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the Cartesian equation of $x=4-t^2$, $y=t^2-3$. Explain why $x\le4$ and $y\ge-3$ and sketch the curve.

answer.short: $x+y=1$, with $x\le4$ and $y\ge-3$: a ray with closed endpoint $(4,-3)$ extending towards the upper left.
answer.worked:
From $x=4-t^2$,
$$t^2=4-x.$$
Substituting into $y=t^2-3$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=(4-x)-3\\y&=1-x\\x+y&=1.\end{aligned}$$
Since $t^2\ge0$,
$$\begin{aligned}x&=4-t^2\le4,\\y&=t^2-3\ge-3.\end{aligned}$$
The graph is the ray on $x+y=1$ with closed endpoint $(4,-3)$, extending towards the upper left.

spec.description: Ray with filled endpoint (4,-3), upper-left continuation arrow, unit intercept ticks and dashed projections to 4 and -3. Ordinary source-blue marks use house black.
